zephyr-client-fixed.built_as: the fixed-memory client of overlays/t2g_client_fixed.conf with the idle wait and batching off (main stack 5696 bytes), its node wz_session_mcu::slot_node
zephyr-client-fixed.chain_misses: calls through a register (7 on the path of the chain), which the stack gate's reader does not follow; the firmware's own reading is 76 bytes over the chain (it was 24 before the connect manager's actions and a new row were built in the places they are kept, which took the dial off the longest chain and left the key matching under a query's answer, and 104 before the received handshake chain kept only the entries the build reads, which moved the path that sets the reading back to the dial, and 76 before the session's bundle was written in its slot field by field, which moved the path that sets the reading from the dial to the handshake's parse, and 108 before the receive decoded into a slot it was lent, 268 before the connect manager's actions were one buffer, and 424 before the dial handed the slot the function that makes the session's parameters, which took 500 from the chain and none from the reading, because the reading was on the planner's path; see the measured note), since the initial sequence number stopped taking the permutation's frame (CONFIG_WZ_INITIAL_SN_COMPACT) and the connect manager's planner call became a trait object, and the path that sets the reading was not identified
zephyr-client-fixed.measured: 2026-10-23, the T2G kit (CYT4BF M7) on its own Ethernet to a zenohd on the bench host; the stack line is the same in 7 of 7 runs, the GET figure is the median of 14 medians (0.320 to 0.471 ms) of 2000 queries for each of the node's two documents. The stack figures were re-read on 2026-10-27 after the not-a-Frame dispatch was split into decode, judge and engine steps (static chain 6,940, peak 6,060 in 2 of 2 runs, GETs inside their row; the tree before the split read 7,152 and 6,336, and the one before log_args 7,296 and 6,480): the decoded handshake message no longer sits in a frame under the engine's answer, and the worst chain is now the connect manager's dial path. After the SCE pin moved to 6dbfa6a521 the same build read static chain 6,372 and peak 5,880 in 2 of 2 runs (the engine's microstep buffers are sized to each document's state tree). On 2026-10-28 the five declarations a session with no allocator sends went through one dispatch, taking the arguments of their writer in place of a closure each (text 176,352 to 174,100 bytes): the worst chain reads 6,396 and the peak 5,904 in 1 of 1 run, 24 bytes over the row, 16 of them the enum the main frame now holds. On 2026-10-28 the initial sequence number became a compact function of the two zids (`CONFIG_WZ_INITIAL_SN_COMPACT`, which this image's overlay turns on): the Keccak permutation was the deepest frame of the chain, which fell 500 bytes to 5,896 (17 frames, 12 calls through a register not followed), and the kit's reading did not move, 5,904 in 1 of 1 run, GETs answered by a zenohd with the new origin. On 2026-10-28 the connect manager's `drive` and `ask` took the planner's call as a trait object (one copy each and not one per closure): the chain fell to 5,512 (the main frame 1,792 to 1,256) and the peak read 5,904 as before, in 1 of 1 run. On 2026-10-28 the dial handed the slot the function that makes the session's parameters (328 bytes, which each call between the dial and the slot had copied into its frame): the chain fell to 4,980 (`dial_expecting` 1,224 to 688), the bound to 6,084 (the worst path is now the planner's `open` and the peer entry, 1,000 and 1,080 bytes), and the peak read 5,904 as before, in 1 of 1 run; the main stack follows the bound, 8,320 to 8,128. On 2026-10-28 the connect manager's peer entry was built as the call's own result and started after it was in the table (`PeerEntry::new` no longer starts a local machine and moves it): the reading, which sat on the planner's path and not on the dial's, fell 656 bytes to 5,248 in 1 of 1 run, and the bound to 5,972 (the worst path is now the receive's lend of a declaration, 2,064 bytes, under a query's answer); the main stack follows, 8,128 to 8,000. On 2026-10-29 the connect manager's actions became one buffer that `drive` fills through `ask` and `take` reads in place (the six of them, about 300 bytes, had been a copy in `ask`, one in `drive` and one more for `take`), and `reconcile` put the rows in the list's order in place (it had held two copies of the table): the chain fell to 4,172 (the receive's, now) and the reading 1,000 bytes to 4,280 in 1 of 1 run; the bound stays 5,972, set by the receive's lend of a declaration. On 2026-10-29 the loop's node (448 bytes), factory (68) and host (36) were built in the storage's arena (`NodeStorage::run`, 576 bytes of `.bss`) and not held as locals of the main function (704 bytes of frame, from 1,256): the chain fell to 3,620, the reading 552 bytes to 3,728 in 1 of 1 run, the bound to 5,420; the main stack follows, 8,000 to 7,232. On 2026-10-29 the receive decoded a transport message into a slot its caller lends (`parse_unit_into`, `decode_unit_in` and `decide_unit_in` take the slot; they had passed the 720-byte message by value, and `parse_init` built it in a local of its own beside the caller's): the handshake's parse, 1,008 bytes of frame, is no longer the worst chain; the dial is (`reconcile`, `drive`, `dial_peer`, `dial_expecting` and the slot's `open`, 3,564 bytes over 7 frames), and the reading fell 88 bytes to 3,640 in 1 of 1 run. On 2026-10-29 four more changes of the same kind: the dial's link made in the slot's claim (`claim_with`; the 176-byte driver was held in several copies in `dial_expecting`, 688 bytes of frame, now 256), the receive's records decoded in the binding that lends them (`lend_declare` 2,064 bytes and `lend_push` 1,776 were three copies of the largest message a record can be; the generated `decode_into` writes it once), the key matcher's view of a key one array on this profile (256 bytes, where it was over 400) and the peer table's entry built in its row (`PeerEntry::init_in`, over the machine's `new_in_place`: the planner's `open` held the machine's kilobyte as a temporary, 1,008 bytes of frame, now 200): the chain 3,132, the bound 4,240 and the reading 3,208 in 1 of 1 run (it was 3,584 until the planner's, which the first dial runs through). On 2026-10-29 the session's bundle was written in the slot field by field (`SessionLinkActions::build_in`; the four handshake ext chains, 200 bytes each, were four slots of the frame of the function that built it, and the bundle had been a value of that function): the slot's `open` and what it calls fell from 1,068 bytes to about 570, the first tick's reading to 3,048, and the worst chain of direct calls is now the handshake's parse (the receive of an Init, 3,088 bytes), which sets the reading at 3,192 in 1 of 1 run. On 2026-10-29 a received handshake message kept the entries of the extensions the build reads and the header byte of every entry, where it had kept up to eight entries of 65 bytes (`ReceivedExtChain`: the inbound frame the decoder is lent fell by some 330 bytes, and `dispatch_unit_borrowed`, `parse_init` and the chain reader with it): the chain 3,024, the dial's path (the session pump's `build_in`, the engine's microsteps and `send_open_syn`) is the longest again, and the reading is 3,048 in 1 of 1 run, the first tick's. On 2026-10-29 the connect manager's actions (248 bytes, a local of `drive`) became a field of the manager, which lives in the node's storage (`RUN` 576 to 832 bytes, `.bss` 256 bytes more), and a new row was built in the table's row (`BoundedVec::push_with`, over a 152-byte value held twice in `reconcile`): the dial is off the longest chain, which is the key matching under a query's answer now (`dispatch_event_among`, `keyexpr_intersects_text`, `keyexpr_intersects_target`), 2,812 bytes, and the reading is 2,888 in 1 of 1 run, as many bytes as the single-thread zenoh-pico image's main thread.

zephyr-client-fixed-batching.built_as: the fixed-memory client of overlays/t2g_client_batching.conf with one send window sent as one datagram, the idle wait off (main stack 5696 bytes), its node wz_session_mcu::slot_node
zephyr-client-fixed-batching.chain_misses: calls through a register (7 on the path of the chain), which the stack gate's reader does not follow; the firmware's own reading is 76 bytes over the chain (it was 24 before the connect manager's actions and a new row were built in the places they are kept, which took the dial off the longest chain and left the key matching under a query's answer, and 104 before the received handshake chain kept only the entries the build reads, which moved the path that sets the reading back to the dial, and 76 before the session's bundle was written in its slot field by field, which moved the path that sets the reading from the dial to the handshake's parse, and 108 before the receive decoded into a slot it was lent, 244 before the connect manager's actions were one buffer, and 428 before the dial handed the slot the function that makes the session's parameters, which took 476 from the chain and none from the reading, because the reading was on the planner's path; see the measured note), since the initial sequence number stopped taking the permutation's frame (CONFIG_WZ_INITIAL_SN_COMPACT) and the connect manager's planner call became a trait object, and the path that sets the reading was not identified
zephyr-client-fixed-batching.measured: 2026-10-23, the T2G kit (CYT4BF M7) on its own Ethernet to a zenohd on the bench host; the stack line is the same in 3 of 3 runs, the GET figure is the median of 6 medians (0.287 to 0.462 ms) of 2000 queries for each of the node's two documents. The two stack figures were re-measured on 2026-10-27 (static chain 7460, peak 6328 in 3 of 3 runs) and moved from 7204 and 6016: the slot node keeps the latest sample of a subscription (chain +136) and holds sessions a peer opened beside the dialled ones (+64), the connect manager is held by the shared planner and by nodes' zids (+88), a few smaller steps, and the log lines are no longer inlined into the main frame (-144); on 2026-10-27 the not-a-Frame dispatch was split into decode, judge and engine steps and the two read 6940 and 6060 in 2 of 2 runs (the worst chain is now the connect manager's dial path); after the SCE pin moved to 6dbfa6a521 they read 6372 and 5904 in 2 of 2 runs; on 2026-10-28 the five declarations a session with no allocator sends went through one dispatch (this image's text is 178,652 bytes after it) and the peak reads 5,928 in 1 of 1 run; the GET figure was not re-measured. On 2026-10-28 the initial sequence number became a compact function of the two zids (see the fixed client's row): the chain fell to 5,904 and the peak did not move, 5,928 in 1 of 1 run. The connect manager's planner call then became a trait object (see the fixed client's row): the chain 5,520 and the peak 5,908 in 3 of 3 runs (the first read a GET median of 492 us, outside the row, and the two runs after it did not). The peer entry built as the call's own result (see the fixed client's row): the peak 5,248 in 1 of 1 run, the bound 5,972, the main stack 8,000. The connect manager's actions as one buffer and its rows reordered in place (see the fixed client's row): the chain 4,172 and the peak 4,280 in 1 of 1 run. The loop's state built in the storage's arena (see the fixed client's row): the chain 3,620 and the peak 3,728 in 1 of 1 run, the bound 5,420, the main stack 7,232. The receive decoding into a slot it is lent (see the fixed client's row): the chain 3,588 and the peak 3,664 in 1 of 1 run. The four changes of 2026-10-29 listed at the fixed client's row: the chain 3,156 and the peak 3,232 in 1 of 1 run, the bound 4,240, the main stack 5,696. The bundle written in its slot field by field (see the fixed client's row): the chain 3,088 and the peak 3,192 in 1 of 1 run. The received handshake chain keeping the entries the build reads (see the fixed client's row): the chain 3,024 and the peak 3,048 in 1 of 1 run. The connect manager's actions built in its storage and a row built in the table (see the fixed client's row): the chain 2,812 and the peak 2,888 in 1 of 1 run

zephyr-client-fixed-get.built_as: the fixed-memory client of overlays/t2g_client_get.conf, which also asks one query at a time (two pending rows), the idle wait and batching off (main stack 6720 bytes); its node is wz_session_mcu::slot_node and its getter wz_session_mcu::slot_getter
zephyr-client-fixed-get.chain_misses: the reply sink and the reply view are called through a register (11 such calls on the path of the chain), which the stack gate's reader does not follow; the firmware's own reading is 544 bytes over the chain
zephyr-client-fixed-get.measured: 2026-10-23, the T2G kit (CYT4BF M7) asking a responder on the bench host, a client of a zenohd there, for a document of 165 bytes, 2050 queries with 50 of warm-up; the stack line and the getter's median (300 us, p99 1300 to 1400 us) are the same in 8 of 8 clean runs; the kernel tick is 100 us, so the median has that resolution. The two stack figures were re-measured on 2026-10-27 (static chain 7784, peak 8328 in 3 of 3 runs) and moved from 7672 and 8144; the changes on this path since 2026-10-23 are those named in the batching row, and this image's own share of them was not bisected; the same day the not-a-Frame dispatch was split into decode, judge and engine steps and the two read 7092 and 6648 in 2 of 2 runs (the reading was under the chain, so the `chain_misses` key was gone for that build); after the SCE pin moved to 6dbfa6a521 the chain reads 6524 and the reading is the same 6648 in 2 of 2 runs, so the reading is 124 bytes over the chain again and `chain_misses` is back. The chain fell 568 and the reading did not move, so the path that sets this peak is not the one the pin shortened; which it is was not found, and the calls through a register on the path (10) are where the reader stops; the getter's median was not re-measured; after the numbers and the console lines were written without core::fmt (the image's text is 185,432 bytes at that point and 185,768 with the polling path in the ITCM) the chain reads 6492 and the reading 6600 in 2 of 2 runs, 48 bytes lower, so the reading is 108 bytes over the chain; the getter's median was not re-measured. On 2026-10-28 the connect manager's planner call became a trait object: the chain reads 5,768 and the reading 6,160 in 1 of 1 run, 440 bytes lower, and the getter's median stayed inside its row. On 2026-10-28 the session's link driver was named by its type: the chain stayed 5,768 and the reading fell 48 bytes to 6,112 in 1 of 1 run, and the getter's median stayed inside its row. On 2026-10-28 the receive handed a lent record to its own callee and the getter asked only on the turn's own event: the chain stayed 5,768 and the reading fell 92 bytes to 6,020 in 1 of 1 run, the queries were asked and answered, and the getter's median stayed inside its row. The peer entry built as the call's own result (see the fixed client's row): the reading fell 660 bytes to 5,360 in 1 of 1 run; the bound stays 6,768 (its worst path is the receive's lend of a declaration under a query's answer, which this change does not touch) and so does the main stack; the queries were asked and answered with no wz: FAIL line and the run is inside its row. The connect manager's actions as one buffer and its rows reordered in place (see the fixed client's row): the chain 4,756 and the reading 5,104 in 1 of 1 run, the queries asked and answered with no wz: FAIL line. On 2026-10-29 the records decoded in the binding that lends them and the key matcher's view of a key one array (see the fixed client's row): the chain 4,008, the bound 5,036, the main stack 6,720, and the reading did not move, 4,552 (the path that sets it was not looked at). Before those, on 2026-10-29 the loop's node, factory and host were built in the storage's arena (`NodeStorage::run`) and no longer held as locals of the main function (task entry 1,368 to 816 bytes): the chain 4,204, the reading 4,552 and the bound 6,216 in 1 of 1 run, the main stack 9,024 to 8,320

zephyr-client-fixed-tls.built_as: the fixed-memory client of overlays/t2g_client_tls.conf, which dials tls/ over Zephyr's TCP with the secure channel (wz-tls-mbedtls on Zephyr's Mbed TLS 4.1.0, mutual TLS 1.3, its 49,152-byte arena), the idle wait and batching off (main stack 12288 bytes), its node wz_session_mcu::slot_node
zephyr-client-fixed-tls.measured: 2026-10-24, the T2G kit (CYT4BF M7) on its own Ethernet to a zenohd 1.10.1 on the bench host that pins the image's certificate and is verified by it; the stack line is the same in 8 of 8 runs, the GET figure is the median of 8 medians (0.583 to 0.765 ms) of 2000 queries for each of the node's two documents; the client without the channel, run in turn with it, gave medians of 0.395 to 0.472 ms. The two stack figures were re-read on 2026-10-27 (static chain 7432 and peak 6752 in 2 of 2 runs, session established, peer verified) and moved from 7016 and 6864: the peak fell 112 with the split of the not-a-Frame dispatch into decode, judge and engine steps, and the chain, 7432 with and without that split, rose 416 with the connect manager's dial path since 2026-10-24, which was not bisected; after the SCE pin moved to 6dbfa6a521 the chain is the same 7432 and the peak reads 6688 in 2 of 2 runs; the GET figure was not re-measured
